title: 20. Volume and Surface Area of Solids

q.t: Find the volume of a cuboid 5 cm × 4 cm × 3 cm (in cm³).
q.e: Each layer holds 5 × 4 = 20 unit cubes and there are 3 layers: 60.

q.t: Find the volume of a cube of side 4 cm (in cm³).
q.e: side × side × side.

q.t: Find the total surface area of a cube of side 3 cm (in cm²).
q.e: Six square faces of 9 cm² each.

q.t: The volume of a cylinder with radius r and height h is:
q.e: Area of the circular base (πr²) × height — a stack of circles.

q.t: How many cubic centimetres make 1 litre?
q.e: A litre fills a cube 10 cm × 10 cm × 10 cm.

q.t: Find the total surface area of a cuboid 3 cm × 2 cm × 1 cm (in cm²).
q.e: Three pairs of faces: 2 × (6 + 2 + 3) = 22.

q.t: How many litres does 1 cubic metre hold?
Find the lateral surface area (4 walls) of a cube of side 5 cm (in cm²).
q.e: Four side faces of 25 cm² each (top and bottom left out).

q.t: The curved surface area of a cylinder is:
q.e: Unroll the curved surface into a rectangle: its length is the circumference 2πr and its width is h.

q.t: Find the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm (take π = 22/7), in cm³.
A cuboid has volume 240 cm³, length 8 cm and breadth 6 cm. Find its height (in cm).
q.e: Height = volume ÷ base area = 240 ÷ 48 = 5.

q.t: A cube has total surface area 150 cm². Find its side (in cm).
q.e: 6a² = 150, so a² = 25 and a = 5.

q.t: Find the curved surface area of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 20 cm (take π = 22/7), in cm².
Find the total surface area of a closed cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 8 cm (take π = 22/7), in cm².
q.e: 2πr(r + h) = 44 × 15 = 660 — the curved surface plus the two circular ends.

q.t: A tank is 2 m × 1.5 m × 1 m. How many litres of water does it hold?
q.e: Volume = 3 m³, and 1 m³ = 1000 litres.

q.t: A cube has volume 343 cm³. Find its total surface area (in cm²).
q.e: Side = ∛343 = 7. Surface area = 6 × 49 = 294.

q.t: A cylinder has volume 1232 cm³ and radius 7 cm. Find its height (take π = 22/7), in cm.
q.e: Base area = 154 cm². Height = 1232 ÷ 154 = 8.

q.t: Find the length of the longest rod that fits in a box 12 cm × 4 cm × 3 cm (in cm).
q.e: The space diagonal: √(12² + 4² + 3²) = √169 = 13.

q.t: How many cubes of side 5 cm can be cut from a cuboid 20 cm × 15 cm × 10 cm?
q.e: 4 along the length, 3 along the breadth, 2 along the height: 24.

q.t: A room is 6 m long, 5 m wide and 4 m high. Find the area of its four walls (in m²).
q.e: Perimeter of the floor × height = 22 × 4 = 88.

q.t: Three cubes of side 6 cm are joined end to end. Find the total surface area of the cuboid formed (in cm²).
q.e: The cuboid is 18 × 6 × 6: 2 × (108 + 36 + 108) = 504. (Four inner faces are hidden, so it is less than 3 × 216.)

q.t: The radius of a cylinder is doubled and its height is halved. Its volume:
q.e: πr²h becomes π(2r)²(h/2) = 2πr²h. The radius is squared, so doubling it counts four-fold.

q.t: A rectangular sheet 44 cm × 20 cm is rolled along its length into a cylinder of height 20 cm. Find its volume (take π = 22/7), in cm³.
q.e: The 44 cm edge becomes the circumference: 2 × 22/7 × r = 44, so r = 7. Volume = 154 × 20 = 3080.

q.t: A well of diameter 7 m is dug 20 m deep. Find the volume of earth dug out (take π = 22/7), in m³.
A hollow pipe is 21 cm long with outer radius 4 cm and inner radius 3 cm. Find the volume of metal (take π = 22/7), in cm³.
q.e: Outer cylinder minus inner cylinder: π(4² − 3²) × 21 = 22/7 × 7 × 21 = 462.

q.t: The edges of a cuboid are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 and its total surface area is 88 cm². Find its volume (in cm³).
q.e: 2(2 + 6 + 3)k² = 22k² = 88, so k = 2. Edges 2, 4, 6: volume 48.

q.t: Three metal cubes of edges 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm are melted into one cube. Find its edge (in cm).
A road roller is 1 m long with diameter 84 cm. What area does it level in 500 complete turns (take π = 22/7), in m²?
q.e: One turn covers its curved surface: 22/7 × 0.84 × 1 = 2.64 m². 500 turns: 1320 m².

q.t: A river 3 m deep and 40 m wide flows at 2 km/h. How much water passes a point in one minute (in m³)?
q.e: In one minute the water moves 2000 ÷ 60 m. Volume = that length × 3 × 40 = 4000 m³.

q.t: How many bricks 25 cm × 10 cm × 8 cm are needed for a wall 5 m × 3 m × 20 cm?
A cylinder has curved surface area 1320 cm² and base circumference 44 cm. Find its volume (take π = 22/7), in cm³.
q.e: Height = 1320 ÷ 44 = 30. Circumference 44 gives r = 7. Volume = 154 × 30 = 4620.

q.t: The length, breadth and height of a cuboid add up to 19 cm and its space diagonal is 11 cm. Find its total surface area (in cm²).
q.e: (l + b + h)² = l² + b² + h² + 2(lb + bh + hl). So the surface area = 361 − 121 = 240.

q.t: A cube has surface area 216 cm². Each side is increased by 50%. Find the new volume (in cm³).
q.e: 6a² = 216 gives a = 6. New side = 9, and 9³ = 729.

q.t: A cylindrical tank has radius 1.4 m and height 2 m. Find its capacity in litres (take π = 22/7).
2 cm of rain falls on a field of 1 hectare. Find the volume of water that falls (in m³).
q.e: 1 hectare = 10,000 m² and 2 cm = 0.02 m. Volume = 200 m³.

q.t: The largest possible cylinder is cut from a cube of side 14 cm. Find its volume (take π = 22/7), in cm³.
q.e: Its diameter and height both equal 14: r = 7, h = 14. Volume = 154 × 14 = 2156.

q.t: Two cylinders have radii in the ratio 2 : 3 and heights in the ratio 5 : 3. Find the ratio of their volumes.
Squares of side 3 cm are cut from each corner of a sheet 24 cm × 18 cm and the sides folded up to make an open box. Find its volume (in cm³).
q.e: Each dimension loses 3 cm at both ends: 18 × 12, with height 3. Volume = 648.

q.t: A room is 8 m × 6 m × 3 m. Find the cost of painting its four walls and ceiling at ₹20 per m² (in ₹).
q.e: Walls: 2 × 14 × 3 = 84 m². Ceiling: 48 m². Total 132 m² × 20 = 2640.

q.t: Water flows at 0.7 m/s through a pipe of radius 1 cm into a cylindrical tank of radius 40 cm. By how much does the water level rise in 30 minutes (in cm)?
q.e: Water in = π × 1² × (70 cm/s × 1800 s). Rise = that ÷ (π × 40²) = 1,26,000 ÷ 1600 = 78.75 cm. The π cancels.
